deaCaptured","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a06742-6f9a-7449-89b2-9bebefe71721\u0022,\u0022OwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022Text\u0022:\u0022A hall9k node runs inside a container, deployable pretty much anywhere (an Azure container app, a local Docker container), and nodes manage each other peer-to-peer: an orchestrator mode on one node (say, the laptop) distributes work across all the others, assigning to a specific node with capacity or auto-assigning to whichever has capacity, where capacity means both the node\\u0027s compute and the subscription it runs on, its token budget, how much it can be burning. Two hard problems captured at the start (Brian, 2026-09-03): (1) the CLI is the agent harness, so the container has to authenticate its CLI to the model provider to spawn agent sessions at all: what does credentialing a headless containerized Claude Code, or any runtime, look like, and how does an operator configure a fresh container to become THEIR node (SSH in? a setup surface?); (2) node-to-node management as a real distributed system: peer-to-peer, work distribution, capacity reporting.
